paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No.91 of 2004
Ishwar,
S/o Shri Ram Kishan,
R/o Indresh Nagar,
Police Station Kotwali, Dehradun
District Dehradun .......Appellant
 Versus
State of Uttaranchal (Now State of Uttarakhand)
 .......Respondent
Mr. Lokendra Dobhal, learned counsel for the appellant.
Mr. Raman Kumar Shah, learned A.G.A. with Ms. Sangeeta Miyan, learned Brief
Holder for the State.
Dated: May 9, 2013
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
This appeal, preferred under Section 374 (2) of
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short Cr.P.C.), is
directed against the judgment and order dated
20.02.2004, passed by the Additional Sessions Judge/
7th Fast Track Court, Dehradun, in Sessions Trial No.
192 of 2000, whereby the said court has convicted
accused/appellant Ishwar under Section 366 & 376 of
I.P.C. The accused/appellant Ishwar has been
sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for a period of
seven years and directed to pay fine of ` 1,000/- under
section 366 of I.P.C., and rigorous imprisonment for a
period of seven years and directed to pay fine of
` 1,000/- under section 376 of I.P.C.

2
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the lower court record.
3. Prosecution story, in brief, is that on 24.07.1999
at 1:20 p.m. P.W.2 Smt. Soniya (daughter of P.W.3
Satya Pal) was kidnapped by the accused Ishwar from
Kanwali Road, Near Post Office, Dehradun. Regarding
said incident, report was lodged by P.W.3 Satya Pal on
25.07.1999, with Police Station Kotwali, Dehradun. On
the basis of said report, Chik report (Ex. A-11) was
prepared and a crime no. 480 of 1999 was registered in
respect of offences punishable under section 363 and
366 of I.P.C., against the accused Ishwar. Investigation
was taken up by P.W.5 S.I. R.B. Arya, who interrogated
the witnesses and started investigation. During
investigation, the accused Ishwar was arrested by the
police and the victim was handed over to her father.
After completion of investigation, the said Investigating
Officer submitted charge sheet against the accused
Ishwar, for his trial in respect of offences punishable
under Section 363, 366 and 376 of I.P.C.
4. The Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun, on
receipt of the charge sheet, after giving necessary
copies to the accused, as required under section 207
Cr.P.C., committed the case to the court of Sessions for
trial. After hearing the parties on 16.12.2000, learned
Sessions Judge, Dehradun, framed charge of offences
punishable under section 363, 366 and 376 of I.P.C, to
which the accused Ishwar pleaded not guilty and
claimed to be tried. On this, prosecution got examined
P.W. 1 Dr. Renuka Naithani, P.W. 2 Smt. Soniya (the

3
victim), P.W.3 Satya Pal (father of the victim), P.W.4
Shakti Singh (brother of the victim), P.W.5 S.I. R.B.
Arya (Investigating Officer) and P.W.6 Smt. Deveshwari
Devi. Oral and documentary evidence was put to the
accused under section 313 Cr.P.C., in reply to which
he alleged that the evidence adduced against him is
false. The accused stated that the complainant
Satyapal was demanding ` 3,00,000/- Lakhs for his
discharge in the case and on his denial, the
complainant has given false evidence. After hearing the
parties, the trial court found accused Ishwar guilty of
charge of offences punishable under section 363, 366
and 376 of I.P.C., and convicted him accordingly. After
hearing on sentence, the convict Ishwar was sentenced
to rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven years
and directed to pay fine of ` 1,000/- under section 366
I.P.C., and rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven
years and directed to pay fine of ` 1,000/- under
section 376 I.P.C. Aggrieved by said judgment and
order dated 20.02.2004, passed by the Additional
Sessions Judge/ 7th Fast Track Court, Dehradun, in
Sessions Trial No. 192 of 2000, this appeal is preferred
by the convict.
5. P.W.1 Dr. Renuka Naithani, medically examined
Smt. Soniya (P.W.2), on 30.07.1999. In the medical
report (Ex. A1-2), she gave following observations:
"No marks of injury seen on her body.
Breast well developed. Auxiliary pubic
hair well developed. Local exam- no
marks of injury seen on her private
parts. Vagina hymen torned old. Vagina

4
admits 2 fingers easily. Vaginal swab
taken and sent for histopathology
exam."
The medical officer opined in her report that no
definite opinion regarding rape could be given at that
moment and submitted that final report would be given
after seeing histopathological report. Regarding age,
girl was advised plain X-Ray knee, ankle, wrist and
elbow joints.
A supplementary medical report was also filed by
P.W.1, in which she opined that no sperm was seen in
her vagina, so regarding rape no definite opinion could
be given. After having examined the X-Ray reports, she
opined that the age of the girl was between 16 & 17
years.
6. P.W.2 Smt. Soniya (victim) has stated that on the
day of incident, when she was returning back from her
school, at about 1:00 p.m., the accused Ishwar
forcefully kidnapped her and took her in a car to his
relatives place. She stated that the accused raped her
without her consent. She also stated that the police
rescued her from near the Railway Station after 4-5
days of the incident. About her age, she stated that at
the time of incident she was 12-13 years old. She also
stated that she was studying in class-6 in Rampyari
School. According to this witness, the S.I. took her
statement and she was sent for medical examination to
the Doon Hospital.
7. P.W.3 Staya Pal (father of the victim) has
corroborated the fact that at the time of incident, his

5
daughter was 13 years old. He stated that on the day of
the incident, his daughter was studying in class-6,
whereas his son Shakti was studying in class-3rd. On
that day, his son and daughter went to the school but
his daughter did not come back. When he returned
back to his home at 5:00 p.m., his wife and son told
him that the accused Ishwar had taken away his
daughter. He searched for her for two days, but when
he could not find her, then he reported the incident to
the police. He further stated that within five days, his
daughter was returned to him by the police.
8. P.W.4 Shakti Singh (brother of the victim) has
stated that he is younger brother of the victim and was
aged 10 years and was studying in class IIIrd at the
time of the incident. He stated that he and his sister
used to go to the Rampyari School together. He stated
that on the day of incident, when he and his sister
were returning from the school at about 1:00 p.m. near
the post office, the accused Ishwar called his sister and
suddenly pushed his sister inside the car. He stated
that both of them screamed, but there was no one on
the road. He stated that he came back home and told
his parents about the kidnapping of his sister.
9. P.W.6 Smt. Deveshwari Devi is the teacher in
Rampyari Kanya Pathshala, Dehradun. She brought
original student entrance registration register in which
at registration no.1132 the name of Km. Sonia D/o
Satya Pal Sigh R/o 243 Patel Nagar, Dehradun is
registered and the date of birth shown is 03.04.1987,
and it is also shown that Km. Sonia had been admitted

6
in class VIth on 10.07.1995. She proved Ext-A-13,
which pertains to the admission and transfer certificate
of the victim, certifying the date of birth of the victim as
03.04.1987.
10. Shri Lokendra Dobhal, learned counsel for the
appellant submitted that the alleged incident took
place on 24.07.1999 in day time, but the First
Information Report of the said incident was lodged on
25.07.1999, which creates a doubt about the conduct
of prosecution. According to him, lodging of report was
an after thought. Further, the alleged incident took
place in the daytime, but no independent witness has
been produced by the prosecution in support of its
case. He further submitted that there is material
contradiction in the statement of prosecution's
witnesses, but the same have not been considered by
the learned trial Court, while convicting the appellant.
P.W.2 Km. Sonia has stated in her statement under
Section 164 Cr.P.C. that she was recovered on
28.07.1999 from a village of District Saharanpur in
presence of her father and police, but in her
examination-in-chief she has stated that police has
recovered her from the clutches of accused from the
Railway Station. Learned counsel for the appellant
submitted that this contradiction in her statement
creates a doubt over the prosecution's story. He further
submitted that P.W.1 Dr. Renuka Naithani has clearly
stated that no mark of injury was found in any part of
person of prosecutrix Soniya and according to her, the
prosecutrix Soniya was aged about 16-17 years at the

7
time of alleged incident and her hymen was found
torned and vagina admitted two fingers easily. In
medical report, no spermatozoa was seen in vaginal
smear examination. Doctor also stated that no definite
opinion could be given about rape. He submitted that
the medical report of prosecutrix Soniya does not
support the version of prosecution and at the most, it
can be said that prosecutrix Soniya was a consenting
party and the appellant has falsely been implicated in
the case. He then submitted that as per the medical
report, at the time of incident the age of prosecutrix
Soniya was about 16-17 years. The prosecution has
not examined the mother of prosecutrix Soniya to know
the actual age of prosecutrix Soniya, which creates
doubt over the conduct of prosecution. He submitted
that in the matter reported in (2005) 13 S.C.C. 376:
Juhi Devi Vs. State of Bihar and others, where the
medical report of medical board showed the girl
between 16 and 17 years whereas the father of the girl
produced a certificate showing the girl minor, the
Hon'ble Supreme Court believing the medical board's
report found the girl as major. He also relied on the
judgment of the Allahabad High Court, reported in
Allahabad Criminal Cases 2001 Vol. 1 (42) page No. 79
Mohd. Kaloo alias Mohd. Jubeel Vs. State of U.P., in
which the Allahabad High Court observed that it is
common knowledge that while describing the date of
birth parents sometimes get reduced the age of their
children in the schools for the purpose of employment,
marriage etc. He further submitted that the Hon'ble
Supreme Court in several judgments has held that in

8
medical examination one should only point out the
approximate age with a possible variation of two years.
He submitted that P.W.-1 Dr. Renuka Nathani has
specifically stated that the prosecutrix was habitual for
intercourse and no definite opinion could be given
regarding the rape and the prosecutrix was between 16
and 17 years. In her statement, she has stated that
one-year difference can be made, therefore, it should be
presumed that the prosecutrix was more than 18 years
at the time of alleged incident. According to the Modi's
Medical Jurisprudence also, two years difference may
be accepted. Learned counsel for the appellant then
contended that by adding two years, the age of the
victim comes to more than 18 years. He also contended
that school certificate produced is fabricated to
implicate the appellant. He further argued that the
name of Shakti Singh P.W.-4 was not mentioned in the
First Information Report, whereas it is alleged that the
said witness was an eyewitness of the incident and on
the instigation of said witness, the First Information
Report was lodged against the appellant. Learned
counsel for the appellant submitted that PW-3 Satya
Pal has also stated in his statement that his son, PW-4
Shakti Singh, had not told him that the prosecutrix
had been taken away by the appellant forcibly and he
had also not told him that the prosecutrix had made a
hue and cry at the time of putting her inside the car,
therefore, this fact shows that the prosecutrix was a
consenting party and she had gone with the appellant
with her own sweet will. He then contended that the
prosecutrix Soniya resided with the appellant for 4-5

9
days, but neither she raised her voice to save herself
from the appellant, nor opposed the appellant. This
fact also shows that the prosecutrix Soniya had gone
with the appellant with her sweet will. He contended
that PW-2 Km. Sonia, prosecutrix, was recovered on
28/29-7-1999 and she was handed over to the custody
of her father PW-3 Satya Pal and her statement under
Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded on 31-08-1999, after
one month of recovery, therefore, it is clear that she
was touted by her father and police to give the
statement against the appellant, therefore, this fact
also creates doubt about the prosecution story.
Learned counsel for the appellant lastly argued that as
alleged by the prosecutrix PW-2 Km. Sonia that she
had not changed her clothes for 5 days, and the said
clothes had not been given to the police for
investigation, therefore, this fact also creates doubt
about the prosecution story.
11. On the other hand, Shri Raman Kumar Shah,
learned A.G.A. for the State submitted that as per
school certificate, the date of birth of the victim was
03.04.1987 and on the day of incident she was less
than 13 years. In such circumstances, consent of the
victim cannot help the appellant. He further submitted
that no reason has been disclosed by the defence side
for falsely implicating the appellant.
12. I have considered the submission advanced by the
learned counsel for the parties. The learned counsel for
the appellant, by relying on the statement of the doctor
that the prosecutrix was between 16 and 17 years of

10
age, argued that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in various
judgments has held that a possible variation of two
years on either side can be considered while
determining the age of the victim. He submitted that
since as per the medical examination, the victim was
about 17 years of age and by adding two years, she
becomes more than 18 years, thus, on the date of
incident, she was major. Though, it is true that the
doctor has determined the approximate age of the
victim between 16 and 17 years, but there may be
variation of two years on either side by considering
other evidence. The prosecution has produced the
School Leaving Certificate of the victim, in which the
date of birth of the victim is shown as 03.04.1987.
P.W.6 Smt. Deveshwari Devi is the teacher in the
Rampyari Kanya Pathshala, Dehradun. She brought
the original student entrance registration register, in
which at registration no.1132, the name of the victim is
registered and her date of birth is shown as
03.04.1987. It is also shown that the victim had been
admitted in class VIth on 10.07.1995. She proved Ext-A-13, which pertains to the admission and transfer
certificate of the victim, certifying the date of birth of
the victim as 03.04.1987. The submission of the
learned counsel for the appellant that the date of birth
certificate of the victim is fabricated, cannot be
accepted in view of the fact that the same was proved
by the teacher of the school and also because the date
of birth of the victim was registered as 03.04.1987 on
the day of admission i.e. on 10.07.1995. The date of
birth of the victim was registered four years prior to the

11
date of incident. Therefore, date of birth of the victim
entered in the school register appears to be genuine.
Had the date of birth been entered in the school
register after the date of incident, the argument of the
learned counsel for the appellant would have some
force. Moreover, on the day of incident, the victim was
studying in Class VI. As per School Certificate, she was
12 years 3 months old. Therefore, in normal
circumstances, twelve years old girl can study in Class
VI, but more than 18 years old girl cannot. Therefore,
the two years variance in the age, in the present
circumstances, is given to the lower side of the medical
report and thus it is held that the victim at the time of
incident was less than 16 years of age.
13. Another argument of the learned counsel for the
appellant is that there is contradiction/variation in the
statement of the brother and father of the victim
regarding kidnapping of the victim. He contended that
the father of the victim has nowhere stated that his son
told him that the victim was kidnapped by the
accused/appellant and thus, the story of kidnapping is
concocted. This submission of the learned counsel for
the appellant has no force in view of the categorical
statement of the victim that the accused Ishwar
forcefully kidnapped her in a car and took her to his
relative's place, and also the statement of the brother of
the victim P.W.4 Shakti Singh, who was aged 10 years
and was studying in class IIIrd at the time of the
incident. This child witness has stated that he and his
sister used to go to the Rampyari School together. He

12
stated that on the day of incident, when he and his
sister were returning from the school at about 1:00
p.m., near the post office the accused Ishwar called his
sister and suddenly pushed his sister inside the car.
He stated that both of them screamed, but there was
no one on the road. Thereafter, he came his home and
told his parents about the kidnapping of his sister. No
suggestion was given by the defence side that the
accused has falsely been implicated. The Court has no
reason to disbelieve the statement of this child witness
and of the victim. Why the victim and her younger
brother would tell lie and would falsely implicate the
accused in a case of kidnapping and rape? Answer is
that the testimony of the victim should be believed.
Another argument raised by the learned counsel for the
appellant is that the victim had ample opportunity to
raise alarm as, as per her version, she was rescued
near Railway station, but she did not raise alarm in
presence of public, therefore, in such circumstances, it
cannot be said that she was forcefully taken and raped
against her wish. This argument is not accepted
because of the tender age of the victim. At that time,
she was between 12-13 years old. Incident of
kidnapping and rape was upsetting, surprising and
shocking for her. Due to fear also, she must have kept
quiet. Last argument of learned counsel for the
appellant is that as no sperm was found in her vagina,
no offence is made out against the appellant under
Section 376 of the I.P.C. In support of this submission,
he referred (2010) National Criminal Cases Vol-2 page-359- Gajendra Chandra vs. State of Uttarakhand in

13
which it is held that sperm in the vagina, after
intercourse, has to stay there for sometime. But
considering the fact that the girl was recovered after
five days' of incident and thereafter, her medical was
conducted on sixth day, and also considering the
statement of P.W.2 (victim) that she was raped by the
appellant, this argument of the learned counsel for the
appellant is also not accepted. The statement of the
victim cannot be disbelieved.
14. Accordingly, the appeal preferred by the accused/
appellant Ishwar is hereby dismissed. The conviction
and sentence awarded by the learned Additional
Sessions Judge/7th Fast Track Court, Dehradun in
Sessions Trial No. 192 of 2000 to the accused/
appellant for the offence punishable under Sections
366 and 376 of I.P.C. is affirmed. The period already
spent by the appellant in jail shall be adjusted.
15. The accused/appellant is on bail. His bail-bonds
are hereby cancelled. The accused/appellant Ishwar be
taken in custody immediately to make accused to serve
out the sentence awarded to him. Let a copy of this
judgment alongwith the record of the Court below be
sent to the trial Court.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
Arpan 09.05.2013
